This usually means the accessibility framework marked the service malfunctioning when this app\'s process was killed - which this ROM does on its own schedule - after which it stops binding it. The switch in Settings already reads as on, which is why turning it \"on\" there changes nothing: it has to be switched off and on. Repair does exactly that.

Accessibility is what keeps this app running: an application hosting an enabled accessibility service holds a system binding, so it is not frozen once it leaves the screen. Without it the MCP endpoint goes silent exactly when an agent in another app tries to use it. It is also what provides screen capture, gestures and the view tree without root.
This is also what keeps the app alive: an application hosting an enabled accessibility service holds a system binding, so it is not frozen once it leaves the screen.
Battery optimisation also freezes the process in the background. Grant unrestricted battery use, and on ColorOS also allow background activity for 奈何桥 in the battery settings.

Every tool the agent calls is running the moment it is asked for, with nothing checking it first - root shell commands included. It switches itself off when the time runs out, and a reboot ends it early. This app being killed and restarted does not - this ROM does that on its own, and losing the window to a memory sweep would help nobody.
The approval dialog is the only thing standing between the agent and this device. Hand-off mode takes it away: for a while, every action runs the moment it is asked for.

It is for the case where you are deliberately letting the agent work through a long sequence without you. It is also the mode that can leave the phone unbootable, so it expires by itself and there is no way to make it stick - only to arm it again.

While this is on, everything the agent calls runs immediately. Root shell commands, injected taps and text, code loaded into other apps, screenshots of whatever is on screen - none of it will ask you first.
The root shell is the one thing that could never be switched off, on purpose - it is why this project exists at all. Hand-off mode covers it too.

A command that deletes files, disables a system component or writes to a partition will run exactly as the agent typed it, with nothing in between. That can leave this device unable to boot, and there is no undo - the audit log records what ran, but it cannot put anything back.
Type %1$s below to enable the button. A pocket, a mis-tap or a stray touch cannot do this - only you, reading this, can.

Running a script brings its app to the front, which puts this one in the background. Without the accessibility service the system freezes this app there and the run never finishes. Turn it on, then run again.

Switching one off or deleting it reaches into the app that is running now, not just the record.

This application hosts the 奈何桥 module and is asking to use the device bridge. Allowing it lets the module inside that app receive injected code and report events. It does not by itself grant any device control - every such action still asks you separately.

This app\'s own countermeasures against the system killing it in the background. They are not hooks an agent made: they do not appear on the Hooks page, and they cannot be deleted - only paused. Each one is aimed at the system framework, so a mistake here is a mistake in the process the whole phone runs on.

No countermeasure is written for this system yet. These are written against specific manufacturers\' background-app killers, and this is not one of them. MIUI\'s is being measured; ColorOS\'s is here.

ColorOS force-stops apps behind your back: Athena is what does it, with the reason \'o-stop\', when you swipe an app out of Recents or the screen turns off. This stops it doing that to 奈何桥, and leaves it working normally for every other app. It also guards the probe\'s cgroup freeze: while one holds, HANS - ColorOS\'s cgroup freezer manager - is kept from thawing that app.

HyperOS force-stops apps behind your back, and it has several ways in: one-tap cleanup, cleaning when the screen turns off, cleaning when you swipe an app away. They all finish in the same place inside the system, with a reason of their own - OneKeyClean, LockScreenClean, SwipeUpClean and so on. This stops that happening to 奈何桥, and leaves every other app, and every other reason, exactly as it was.
On - released into the system framework

Two things have to be true before this can work:
1. The module must be scoped in LSPosed to %1$s. That is the process the hook lives in.
2. The phone must have been restarted since that was set, or the module is not actually loaded there and the hook has nothing to attach to.
Once it is on, it can be paused here at any time but not deleted - and the rescue module suspends it on its own if the phone starts failing to boot.
Released. It is in the system framework as soon as the module is loaded there.
This build has no script for that countermeasure.
Paused. Nothing is hooked any more.

A floating button that freezes the app in front, so a screen that would be gone by the time you look - a splash ad, a transient dialog - stays put while it is inspected. Only your tap freezes: the agent can read the frozen state and ask for the release, but it can never start one. The app stays frozen until you press the button again, the agent asks, or the time runs out and a detached root watchdog lets it go.
